questions.q: What does Lightning Data Service (LDS) let a component do without writing any Apex class?
options: Run arbitrary SOQL aggregate queries across multiple objects
Send emails on the user's behalf
Read and write individual records, with field-level security and sharing enforced automatically
Expose a component to Lightning App Builder
questions.explain: LDS is the platform's built-in layer for reading and writing individual records -- enforcing field-level security and sharing automatically -- with no custom Apex class required.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend importing field references from `@salesforce/schema` instead of writing field API names as plain strings?
options: @salesforce/schema references give a compile-time error if a field is renamed or deleted, instead of a silent runtime failure
Plain strings are not supported at all by lightning/uiRecordApi
@salesforce/schema references run faster at runtime than plain strings
Plain strings can only be used with createRecord, never with getRecord
questions.explain: Importing field references gives compile-time safety -- if a referenced field is renamed or deleted, the build fails loudly, instead of the component silently failing at runtime with a plain string.

questions.q: Why can't `createRecord`, `updateRecord`, or `deleteRecord` be used with the @wire decorator?
options: They can be wired; this lesson's examples simply chose not to
lightning/uiRecordApi does not support @wire for any of its functions
@wire only supports functions that take zero parameters
They are side-effecting write operations, which is exactly the category of Apex/LDS call that @wire cannot be used with
questions.explain: Writing data has side effects, and @wire is reserved for cacheable, read-only operations. All three write functions are called imperatively, just like a non-cacheable Apex method would be.

questions.q: What does `lightning-record-edit-form` provide that you'd otherwise have to write yourself with the JavaScript LDS API?
options: Nothing -- it is purely cosmetic markup with no built-in behavior
A guarantee that the record will be deleted instead of updated
Validation, field-level security enforcement, and the actual save, firing an onsuccess or onerror event, all with no JavaScript required
Automatic Apex class generation on deploy
questions.explain: lightning-record-edit-form handles validation, field-level security, and the save operation declaratively, firing onsuccess/onerror events -- all without writing JavaScript createRecord/updateRecord calls directly.

questions.q: If Component A updates a record through LDS and Component B is separately wired to getRecord for that same record, what happens to Component B?
options: Component B is automatically notified through LDS's shared cache and re-renders with the fresh data, with no custom event or message channel required
Nothing -- Component B must manually call refreshApex to see the change
Component B's wire adapter throws an error because the record changed unexpectedly
Component B would need to be destroyed and recreated to see the new data
questions.explain: LDS maintains one shared client-side cache across every component using it. When one LDS-managed write happens, every component wired to that same record is automatically notified and re-renders -- no manual synchronization code needed.
